complications.detail: clip placed on the common bile duct, which traction has tented into the cystic duct line (Stewart-Way class I mechanism)

the structure divided as the cystic duct is the common bile duct, tented into the line of the cystic duct by infundibular traction — the classic visual perceptual illusion (97% of injuries in the Way series are perceptual, 3% technical)

directive: Never clip or divide a tubular structure in the hepatocystic triangle until the Critical View is demonstrated — two and only two structures entering the gallbladder (T2). The dominant injury mechanism is perceptual, not technical (97% of the Way series, T1): the defence is the discipline of the view.

Confirmed or suspected bile duct injury is referred to an experienced hepatobiliary team — a strong guideline recommendation (T3). Do not attempt definitive repair without that expertise; drain, document, refer.
Prophylaxis timing is a system step, not a detail: cefazolin 2 g started within 60 minutes before incision (T7).
